title: refactor: autoHide should be a widget shared behavior, not a component one
body:
The way [autoHide is written](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/7f983d0d6c592de6a091ec2dc5b5df57da151a82/decorators/autoHide.js) is "broken".

It's acknowledging that the React Components are aware of the node they are mounted to (container). While they should not know about it.

It complexifies the implementation of the autoHide feature for nothing nad restrict us to use it on widgets that are bound to react only.

We should move this decorator as a "widget" decorator (shared behavior). And maybe do the right thing => move the decorator call outside of the widget.

comments.body:
@vvo makes me think that maybe if we want to provide such tool on the widget, maybe we should have the render and other methods for the lifecycle be more like function (return something + no side effects) in order to make them composable. Right we can't do that, since we have no about what's going in those methods.

@pixelastic interesting but I don't have a favorite yet :P
Moved the autoHide feature discussion to #303 to avoid us talking too much different things. This one is really only about refactoring and option name change.

@bobylito I guess we should be able to do high order widgets like we do for components. You could wrap a widget and have a render method that call the underlying one when necessary. Dunno if that's possible.
Hard for now I think. We don't have much control over the output, which is not the case when using React.
